blocks.text: The hidden cost of manual drafting

The primary cost of manual drafting is the erosion of billable hours. When you spend two hours a day in your inbox, you are not designing. In a firm of 50 people, this adds up to 100 lost billable hours every single week. This is not just about money. It is about the mental energy required to switch between design and administration. Every time you leave a CAD or BIM environment to answer an email, you lose focus. Returning to that state of flow takes time. This constant context switching is the real driver of burnout in modern architecture.

Drafting workflows often become stuck because of fragmented communication. When project data lives in email chains rather than a central system, you spend hours searching for the latest version of a file or a specific client instruction. This is the chronological list of unstructured text problem. You are forced to act as a manual bridge between different software and stakeholders. When you rely on memory or manual tracking to keep projects moving, errors creep in. These errors lead to rework, which is the most expensive part of any architectural project.

items: Fee compression limits the time you can spend on each project phase.
The industry culture often discourages the use of automated tools.
Reliance on email for project coordination creates data silos.
Manual version control leads to conflicting information across teams.

blocks.text: You can start improving your workflow today without spending money on new tools. First, treat your email as a task list rather than a filing system. Move project documents into a shared folder structure immediately. Use keyboard shortcuts in your existing apps to speed up repetitive actions. For example, learn the specific shortcuts in Archicad or Vectorworks to reduce mouse travel. Standardize your file naming conventions across the whole team. This simple change reduces the time spent searching for files by a significant margin. If you use Excel for schedules, learn to use formulas to automate calculations instead of typing values manually.

If your firm handles sensitive client or project data, always check your internal security policies before using any AI tools. Ensure you are not sharing confidential information with third-party services.
blocks.title: A note on data privacy

blocks.text: How Lazur helps architects on Mac

Lazur acts as a voice-driven assistant that lives in your Mac notch. It helps you manage your workflow by answering questions about your screen and guiding you through complex tasks. You do not need to click through menus to find a command. Just hold Option + Command and ask where a tool is. Lazur will draw a circle around it. This saves you from hunting through deep nested menus in CAD or BIM software. It also helps with drafting text for emails or project notes. You can dictate clean, formatted text directly into any application.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my CAD files directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It provides guidance and answers questions out loud to help you work faster.

faq.question: Is my screen data safe when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only sees your screen while you hold the shortcut key. Audio and screenshots are sent to AI providers to answer your request and are not stored. Your data is never used to train models.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Revit on Mac?
faq.answer: Revit does not run natively on macOS. Since Lazur is a Mac-native tool, it cannot interact with Windows-based virtual machines or remote desktop environments used to run Revit.
